items.stem: A tree casts a shadow 15 m long on the level of ground, when the angle of elevation of the sun is 45°. Find the height of a tree.
items.answer: Let BC be the tree of height h and AB its shadow, with AB = 15 m and ∠BAC = 45°. In right triangle ABC, BC/AB = tan 45° = 1, so BC = AB = 15 m. The height of the tree is 15 m.

items.stem: In Figure, the angles of depressions from the observing positions O₁ and O₂ respectively of the object A are .................. .
items.answer: Draw O₁X parallel to AC. Since ∠O₁AC = 60° is marked at O₁ in the right triangle O₁BC... taking the horizontal through O₁, the angle of depression of A from O₁ is ∠AO₁X = 90° − 60° = 30°. Taking the horizontal through O₂, the angle of depression of A from O₂ equals the alternate angle ∠BAO₂ = 45°. Hence the angles of depression are 30° and 45°.

items.stem: The .......... is the line drawn from the eye of an observer to the point in the object viewed by the observer.
items.answer: The line joining the observer's eye to the point being viewed is called the line of sight.

items.stem: The .......... of an object viewed, is the angle formed by the line of sight with the horizontal when it is above the horizontal level, i.e., the case when we raise our head to look at the object.
items.answer: When the object lies above the horizontal and the head is raised to view it, the angle between the line of sight and the horizontal is called the angle of elevation.

items.stem: The .......... of an object viewed, is the angle formed by the line of sight with the horizontal when it is below the horizontal level, i.e., the case when we lower our head to look at the object.
items.answer: When the object lies below the horizontal and the head is lowered to view it, the angle between the line of sight and the horizontal is called the angle of depression.

items.stem: A ladder, leaning against a wall, makes an angle of 60° with the horizontal. If the foot of the ladder is 2.5 m away from the wall, find the length of the ladder.
items.answer: Let AC be the ladder, C its foot and CB = 2.5 m the distance from the wall, with ∠C = 60°. In right triangle ACB, cos 60° = CB/AC, so 1/2 = 2.5/AC, giving AC = 2 × 2.5 = 5 m. The ladder is 5 m long.

items.stem: In the adjoining figure, the positions of observer and object are marked. The angle of depression is ..........
items.answer: The observer is at O and the object at P. The angle of depression is the angle the line of sight OP makes with the horizontal at the observer, which by alternate angles equals the 30° marked at P between PO and the horizontal. Hence the angle of depression is 30°.

items.stem: If the angle of depression of an object from a 75 m high tower is 30°, then what is the distance of the object from the tower?
items.answer: Let AB = 75 m be the tower and O the object on the ground, with the angle of depression 30°. By alternate angles the angle of elevation at O is also 30°. In right triangle ABO, tan 30° = AB/OB, so 1/√3 = 75/OB, giving OB = 75√3 m. The object is 75√3 m from the tower.

items.stem: The top of two poles of height 20 m and 14 m are connected by a wire. If the wire makes an angle of 30° with the horizontal, then find the length of the wire.
items.answer: Let CD = 20 m be the taller pole and AB = 14 m the shorter one, and let E be the point on CD level with B. Then DE = CD − CE = 20 − 14 = 6 m, and BD is the wire. In right triangle BDE, sin 30° = DE/BD, so 1/2 = 6/BD, giving BD = 12 m. The wire is 12 m long.

items.stem: If the height and length of the shadow of a man are equal, then find the angle of elevation of the sun.
items.answer: Let AB be the man's height and BC his shadow, with AB = BC. In right triangle ABC, tan θ = AB/BC = AB/AB = 1, so θ = 45°. The sun's angle of elevation is 45°.

items.stem: In the given figure, the positions of the observer and the object are mentioned, find the angle of depression?
items.answer: Let C be the observer, A the object and CX the horizontal through C. The line of sight CA makes 60° with the horizontal at A, and by alternate angles ∠XCA = ∠CAB = 60°. Hence the angle of depression is 60°.

items.stem: A circus artist is climbing a 20 m long rope, which is tightly stretched and tied from the top of a vertical pole to the ground. If the angle made by the rope with the ground level is 30°, then what is the height of pole?
items.answer: Let AB be the vertical pole and CA the 20 m rope, with ∠C = 30°. In right triangle ABC, sin 30° = AB/AC, so 1/2 = AB/20, giving AB = 10 m. The pole is 10 m high.

items.stem: The ratio of the length of a rod and its shadow is 1 : √3 then what is the angle of elevation of the sun ?
items.answer: Let the rod AB have length h, so its shadow BC has length √3 h, and let θ be the sun's elevation. In right triangle ABC, tan θ = h/(√3 h) = 1/√3, so θ = 30°. The sun's angle of elevation is 30°.

items.stem: A ladder 15 m long leans against a wall making an angle of 60° with the wall. Find the height of the point where the ladder touches the wall.
items.answer: Let AB = h be the height on the wall and CA = 15 m the ladder, the ladder making 60° with the wall at A. Then h/15 = cos 60° = 1/2, so h = 15 × 1/2 = 7.5 m. The ladder touches the wall 7.5 m above the ground.

items.stem: A pole casts a shadow of length 2√3 m on the ground, when the Sun's elevation is 60°. Find the height of the pole.
items.answer: Let AB = h be the pole and BC = 2√3 m its shadow, with the elevation at C equal to 60°. Then h/(2√3) = tan 60° = √3, so h = 2√3 × √3 = 6 m. The pole is 6 m high.

items.stem: If the length of the ladder placed against a wall is twice the distance between the foot of the ladder and the wall. Find the angle made by the ladder with the horizontal.
items.answer: Let the distance from the foot of the ladder to the wall be x, so the ladder has length 2x. In right triangle ABC with ∠B = 90°, cos A = x/(2x) = 1/2 = cos 60°. Hence A = 60°, so the ladder makes 60° with the horizontal.

items.stem: An observer, 1.7 m tall, is 20√3 m away from a tower. The angle of elevation from the eye of observer to the top of tower is 30°. Find the height of tower.
items.answer: Let the tower AB have height h. The observer's eye is at D, 1.7 m above the ground, and DE = 20√3 m is the horizontal distance, with AE = h − 1.7. In right triangle ADE, tan 30° = (h − 1.7)/(20√3), so 1/√3 = (h − 1.7)/(20√3), giving h − 1.7 = 20. Hence h = 20 + 1.7 = 21.7 m.
items.section_heading: ONE MARK QUESTIONS | Board Term-2 Foreign 2016

items.stem: In the given figure, AB is a 6 m high pole and DC is a ladder inclined at an angle of 60° to the horizontal and reaches up to point D of pole. If AD = 2.54 m, find the length of ladder. ( use √3 = 1.73)
items.answer: AB = 6 m and AD = 2.54 m, so the ladder meets the pole at a height DB = 6 − 2.54 = 3.46 m. In right triangle BCD with ∠B = 90° and ∠C = 60°, sin 60° = BD/DC, so √3/2 = 3.46/DC, giving DC = (3.46 × 2)/√3 = 6.92/1.73 = 4. The ladder is 4 m long.

items.stem: An observer 1.5 m tall is 28.5 m away from a tower 30 m high. Find the angle of elevation of the top of the tower from his eye.
items.answer: The observer's eye A is 1.5 m above the ground and the horizontal distance AC = 28.5 m. The tower is 30 m high, so the part above eye level is BC = 30 − 1.5 = 28.5 m. In right triangle BAC, tan θ = BC/AC = 28.5/28.5 = 1 = tan 45°, so θ = 45°. The angle of elevation is 45°.

items.stem: If the angles of elevation of the top of a tower from two points distant a and b (a > b) from its foot and in the same straight line from it are respectively 30° and 60°, then find the height of the tower.
items.answer: Let the tower AB have height h, with B its foot, D at distance a and C at distance b. From triangle ABD, h/a = tan 30° = 1/√3, so a = √3 h. From triangle ABC, h/b = tan 60° = √3, so b = h/√3. Multiplying, ab = √3 h × h/√3 = h², hence h = √(ab). The height of the tower is √(ab).

items.stem: The angle of depression of a car parked on the road from the top of a 150 m high tower is 30°. Find the distance of the car from the tower (in m).
items.answer: Let AB = 150 m be the tower and C the car, with d = CB the distance sought. The horizontal AX at the top gives, by alternate angles, ∠ACB = ∠CAX = 30°. In right triangle ABC, tan 30° = 150/d, so 1/√3 = 150/d, giving d = 150√3 m. The car is 150√3 m from the tower.
items.section_heading: ONE MARK QUESTIONS | Board Term-2, 2014

items.stem: A pole 6 m high casts a shadow 2√3 m long on the ground, then find the Sun's elevation.
items.answer: Let the Sun's elevation be θ. The pole AB = 6 m and its shadow BC = 2√3 m. In right triangle ABC, tan θ = AB/BC = 6/(2√3) = 3/√3 = √3 = tan 60°, so θ = 60°. The Sun's elevation is 60°.

items.stem: If the altitude of the sun is 60°, what is the height of a tower which casts a shadow of length 30 m ?
items.answer: Let the tower AB have height h and shadow BC = 30 m, with the altitude at C equal to 60°. In right triangle ABC, AB/BC = tan 60°, so h/30 = √3, giving h = 30√3 m. The tower is 30√3 m high.

items.stem: Find the angle of elevation of the top of the tower from the point on the ground which is 30 m away from the foot of the tower of height 10√3 m.
items.answer: Let θ be the angle of elevation, AB = 10√3 m the tower and BC = 30 m the distance on the ground. In right triangle ABC, tan θ = AB/BC = 10√3/30 = 1/√3 = tan 30°, so θ = 30°. The angle of elevation is 30°.
